CTGAN appears only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it is run or engaged with in the body text.
paper-framework-large-scale-synthetic-20.needs: Body text mentioning CTGAN by name was not found in the provided full-text passages; the single body excerpt given did not correspond to the citation context, so engagement level is inferred from reference-list-only appearance.

paper-semi-supervised-learning-framework.summary: This paper proposes a semi-supervised learning framework for employee performance evaluation that combines expert-labeled records with a large pool of unlabeled data, using group-based feature engineering and iterative high-confidence pseudo-labeling to expand labeled data while preserving distributional stability. It reduces reliance on expert labeling and supports fairer performance comparisons across working groups. The CTGAN paper is cited only in passing as an example of GANs struggling to model complex tabular distributions, with no CTGAN code run.
paper-semi-supervised-learning-framework.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so deeper engagement with CTGAN (if any) cannot be ruled out.

paper-systematic-review-long-tailed-2025.summary: A comprehensive survey of long-tailed learning that proposes a new eight-dimensional taxonomy (data balancing, neural architecture, feature enrichment, logits adjustment, loss function, bells and whistles, network optimization, and posthoc processing) and systematically reviews methods within it, also contrasting long-tailed learning with classical imbalance learning. In its discussion of GAN-based tabular data generation methods used in imbalance learning, the survey describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization of continuous attributes via Gaussian mixture modes and its conditional generator with training-by-sampling for discrete attributes, without running it experimentally.

paper-addressing-imbalance-health-synthe.summary: This paper proposes ACVAE, an Auxiliary-guided Conditional Variational Autoencoder enhanced with contrastive learning, combined with an Edited Centroid-Displacement Nearest Neighbor undersampling step, to address class imbalance across 12 health datasets. The method is compared against traditional oversampling techniques and several benchmark machine learning models. CTGAN appears to be cited and likely used as one of the comparison oversampling baselines, though the abstract itself does not name it explicitly.
paper-addressing-imbalance-health-synthe.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run as a baseline synthesizer or only cited in related work, so integration and importance are uncertain.

paper-ensemble-generative-framework-faul.summary: This paper proposes EPSOGAN, an ensemble of multiple GAN variants combined via multi-objective particle swarm optimization to synthesize high-fidelity fault data for photovoltaic diagnostic systems suffering from scarce fault signatures. The ensemble output is tuned using metrics like Maximum Mean Discrepancy, Coverage, Wasserstein Distance, and Mode Score, and is shown to improve diagnostic accuracy up to 99%. The CTGAN paper is cited among the SDV-family works but the abstract gives no detail on whether CTGAN itself is one of the constituent GAN variants run.
paper-ensemble-generative-framework-faul.needs: Full text needed to confirm whether CTGAN is one of the constituent GAN variants actually run in the ensemble, or merely cited as related work.

paper-android-malware-detection-ctgan-20.summary: This conference paper proposes an Android malware detection pipeline that uses CTGAN to synthesize minority-class samples from the CICMalDroid2020 dataset, followed by LightGBM classification with optional feature selection. The authors report that CTGAN-augmented data without feature selection achieved the best accuracy (95.17%), outperforming other configurations. They explicitly state they used 'helper library from SDV that already implemented CTGAN based on previous research: sdv-dev/SDV - Github,' running it with default parameters except for a modified iteration count, making SDV's CTGAN implementation the core data-augmentation engine of the whole empirical study.
paper-android-malware-detection-ctgan-20.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and metadata available, so exact CTGAN implementation (SDV package vs reimplementation) cannot be confirmed.

paper-attention-cnn-bilstm-model-2025.summary: This conference paper proposes a deep-learning intrusion detection system for IoT networks combining CNN, BiLSTM, and an attention mechanism, evaluated on the CICIoT-2023 dataset with 98.73% accuracy for 8-class classification. To address severe class imbalance among attack categories, the authors use CTGAN to synthesize additional samples for minority classes, generating 119,847 synthetic records during preprocessing. CTGAN (from the SDV family) is run directly as the data-augmentation generator feeding the classifier's training pipeline.
paper-attention-cnn-bilstm-model-2025.needs: Unclear whether the authors used the sdv-dev CTGAN package directly or a custom reimplementation; no import/library statement or hyperparameter table given.

paper-augmenting-insufficiently-accruing.summary: This retrospective validation study evaluates whether generative models can synthesize additional patients to compensate for insufficient accrual in oncology clinical trials, using 10 datasets from 9 completed cancer trials with progressively larger fractions of the latest-recruited patients removed and then simulated back in. Four generative approaches -- sequential synthesis with decision trees, a Bayesian network, a GAN, and a VAE -- were compared against bootstrap resampling using replication metrics (decision agreement, estimate agreement, standardized difference, CI overlap) and fidelity metrics. CTGAN and its tabular VAE variant (TVAE), both described using their per-mode normalization and conditional-vector mechanisms, are two of the four generative models run and benchmarked as evaluation subjects, with sequential synthesis ultimately performing best.
paper-augmenting-insufficiently-accruing.needs: Full text describes CTGAN/TVAE mechanisms in standard SDV terminology and reports fidelity results for both, but never explicitly names the sdv-dev/CTGAN package, so it is not fully certain the SDV-family implementation (vs. an independent reimplementation) was run.

paper-disentangled-deep-smoothed-bootstr.summary: This paper addresses Imbalanced Regression (IR) by proposing a Disentangled Deep Smoothed Bootstrap that combines a disentangled β-VAE latent representation with a Smoothed Bootstrap resampling scheme, aiming to generate more relevant synthetic data for rare target values in tabular regression tasks. The method is benchmarked against several standard synthetic data generators on IR benchmark datasets. TVAE, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN are each run as baseline comparators using the SDV Python package, with results showing these general-purpose generators are not well suited to the imbalanced regression problem.

paper-actgan-iot-security-2025.summary: Augments IoT network traffic to give intrusion detectors enough attack examples to learn from. ACTGAN is the generator, a conditional tabular architecture in the CTGAN line rather than the library itself.

paper-fairsyn-edu-diffusion-model-2025.summary: This paper proposes FairSYN-Edu, a diffusion-based synthetic data generator for educational records that jointly optimizes predictive utility, demographic fairness, and differential privacy, evaluated on MOOC, K-12, and LMS datasets with metrics for RMSE, demographic disparity, and membership-inference resistance. It benchmarks its diffusion model against three baseline generators, including CTGAN and Gaussian Copula, across cross-model comparison and ablation tables showing RMSE/fairness/privacy trade-offs. CTGAN, citing Xu et al.'s conditional GAN paper, is run as one of several comparison baselines whose mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are described in the text.
paper-fairsyn-edu-diffusion-model-2025.needs: Not fully clear whether CTGAN was run via the actual sdv-dev/ctgan package or a custom reimplementation, since only the adversarial loss formula is described without library names or hyperparameter listings.

paper-ganbert-fraud-2025.summary: Proposes GAN_BERT, a three-stage pipeline for credit-card fraud detection on a dataset where fraud is a fifth of a percent of rows: CTGAN is trained on the minority class alone to produce synthetic fraud records, a stratified loader mixes real majority, real minority and synthetic rows into balanced batches at configurable ratios, and a FinBERT classifier is fine-tuned on those batches. CTGAN is run unmodified as the generator stage, with the conditional generator and discriminator objectives reproduced from the CTGAN paper, so the named model is a composite built around CTGAN rather than a variant of it; the reported precision and recall gains on the minority class rest on the rows it supplies.

paper-livelihood-capital-behavioral-resp.summary: This study examines how livelihood capital structures shape the annual livelihood strategies of small-scale fishers in Guangdong Province, China, under China's seasonal fishing moratorium, combining regression analysis with agent-based simulation and data augmentation of survey data. It extends the Sustainable Livelihoods Approach by incorporating environmental and psychological capital and identifies threshold effects and heterogeneous temporal impacts of different capital types on fishers' behavioral adaptation. CTGAN is cited several times in the literature review and future-work sections as an example of tabular GAN architectures that can learn joint distributions in mixed-type data, but is not implemented or run in the study's own data augmentation, which the authors instead flag as a direction for future benchmarking.
paper-livelihood-capital-behavioral-resp.needs: The paper's own 'data augmentation' method used in the empirical analysis is never specified as CTGAN or any named library; CTGAN appears only in literature-review and future-work discussion.

paper-optimizing-university-campus-funct.summary: This study proposes a framework combining street-view image semantic segmentation, perception surveys, and interpretable machine learning to compare how students and visitors perceive campus functional zones at a Chinese university, using SHAP-enabled decision trees to quantify landscape feature contributions. To address class imbalance in perception survey scores caused by group-space interactions, the authors apply CTGAN to generate synthetic minority samples for extreme high/low-scoring cases before training their tree ensembles. CTGAN's conditional generation and mode normalization are run as the data augmentation step underlying all six perception-prediction tasks in the empirical pipeline.
paper-optimizing-university-campus-funct.needs: Evidence does not explicitly confirm use of the sdv-dev CTGAN package (no import statement or constructor parameters shown), though usage pattern strongly matches library-based application rather than a from-scratch reimplementation.

paper-predicting-doxorubicin-induced-car.summary: This paper develops a machine learning screening model to predict doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in breast cancer patients, using a small cohort of 78 Brazilian patients augmented with a novel data augmentation and smoothing (DAS) method that leverages routine blood biomarkers and clinical measures. The authors compare DAS against three established oversampling/synthetic data techniques -- SMOTE, ADASYN, and SDV -- training separate predictive models on each method's synthetic output and evaluating AUROC, sensitivity, and specificity. SDV is run as one of several baseline synthetic data generators benchmarked against the proposed DAS method, with SDV ultimately underperforming on AUROC and sensitivity despite higher specificity.
paper-predicting-doxorubicin-induced-car.needs: The specific SDV synthesizer used (e.g., GaussianCopula, CTGAN default) is not named, so sdv_concept is left empty.

paper-preserving-privacy-marketing-compa.summary: This conference paper builds a GAN-based synthetic customer data generator paired with an LLM-driven campaign generation pipeline, comparing marketing campaigns produced from synthetic versus real customer records via automated LLM scoring and a 200-participant human survey. The authors implement two GAN variants for the generator: a standard GAN and their own CTGAN-style architecture that conditions on categorical columns to handle multimodal and imbalanced categorical features. This CTGAN variant is a from-scratch reimplementation of the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN design, not the sdv-dev library, used as one of the two generators evaluated in the empirical comparison.
paper-preserving-privacy-marketing-compa.needs: The reference list cites Patki et al. 2016 (SDV) as [18], but no body-text passage engaging with SDV itself was found; the substantive engagement is with a self-built CTGAN-style architecture rather than the sdv-dev package.

paper-spatial-temporal-correlation-analy.summary: This hydrology study analyzes over 60 years of Yangtze River basin runoff data to model spatiotemporal coincidence risks among floods from tributaries and lakes, using an optimal high-dimensional R-Vine Copula function to quantify dependence structures and assess how the Three Gorges Dam has altered coincidence risk. The work is a domain application in flood-risk hydrology rather than a machine-learning or synthetic-data study. It cites the SDV-family vine-copula paper as a methodological reference for the R-Vine Copula technique it applies to its own flood dataset, without evidence of running any SDV software component.
paper-spatial-temporal-correlation-analy.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether the vine copula citation is a methodological reference only or whether the SDV 'copulas' package was actually used to implement the R-Vine Copula model.

paper-synthetic-factory-scalable-domain-.summary: This conference paper presents a modular, domain-agnostic pipeline for generating synthetic tabular data, combining data preprocessing, synthetic generation, statistical fidelity assessment (Jensen-Shannon divergence, correlation similarity), and ML-utility evaluation across domains such as healthcare, finance, and retail. The entire generation stage of the pipeline is built on CTGAN and Gaussian Copula models, which are trained on real data and sampled to produce the synthetic datasets evaluated throughout the paper. CTGAN and the Gaussian Copula synthesizer -- both part of the SDV family -- are run as the core generators underpinning the whole empirical pipeline, with the original Synthetic Data Vault paper cited as foundational prior work.
paper-synthetic-factory-scalable-domain-.needs: Evidence does not explicitly confirm whether the authors used the sdv-dev/ctgan package directly or a custom reimplementation of CTGAN/Gaussian Copula; no import statements or hyperparameter tables are shown.

paper-synthetic-generation-book-recommen.summary: This paper proposes generating synthetic rating matrices for book recommendation by training a knowledge graph embedding (TransE) on the Goodreads dataset and simulating users' reading behavior via link prediction, then evaluating recommendation precision/recall against real and random-baseline data. The method does not use CTGAN or any SDV-family model; TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is only listed in the reference list as prior work on synthesizing tabular data via GANs. TGAN is cited only bibliographically and never engaged with in the body text.
paper-synthetic-generation-book-recommen.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is run, adapted, or only cited in a related-work list. Industry and use_case inferred solely from the title's mention of book recommendation and synthetic data generation.

paper-synthetic-catalyst-applications-he.summary: A survey-style conference paper reviewing state-of-the-art synthetic data generation methods (GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, transformer approaches) and their applications across healthcare, finance, crime investigation, legal systems, and climate science, alongside discussion of evaluation gaps, bias amplification, and governance. It surveys practical open-source libraries and frameworks rather than running any experiments of its own. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited and briefly described as providing modular tools for tabular, relational, and time-series synthesis, alongside CTGAN/TGAN and YData-Synthetic, purely as prior art discussed in the related-work/library-overview section.
paper-synthetic-catalyst-applications-he.needs: Ref [16], cited as 'CTGAN', is actually Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018 (TGAN); the paper conflates the two names without running either library.

paper-synthetic-driven-asthma-severity-2.summary: This conference paper addresses healthcare data scarcity and privacy concerns in asthma severity classification by first generating synthetic patient data (FEV1, FVC, PEFR) with CTGAN, then training a custom LSTM classifier on that synthetic data to distinguish normal, mild, and severe asthma. The authors report better testing accuracy with larger synthetic datasets and build toward a personalized treatment-plan GUI. They cite SDV's CTGANSynthesizer documentation directly for the model's hyperparameters (epochs, batch size, learning rate, pac), indicating the SDV package's CTGAN implementation is the generator producing all synthetic training data.
paper-synthetic-driven-asthma-severity-2.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a custom reimplementation was used, though phrasing suggests the standard CTGAN model was applied as-is.

paper-machine-learning-pipeline-predicti.summary: This paper develops an end-to-end machine learning pipeline that predicts Pinot Noir grape yield, juice/wine composition, and final wine quality from New Zealand viticulture data, culminating in a web-based prediction application. To address limited training data, the authors use the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package with its FAST_ML preset to generate 6000 synthetic samples that capture correlations and basic statistics (min/max, averages, standard deviations) of the original dataset for data augmentation. SDV's tabular synthesis functionality is run directly as the generator producing augmented training data feeding the ML pipeline.
paper-machine-learning-pipeline-predicti.needs: Specific SDV synthesizer/algorithm underlying FAST_ML preset is not named, so sdv_concept left empty per rules.

paper-epic-effective-prompting-imbalance.summary: EPIC proposes a large-language-model prompting method for generating synthetic samples of minority classes to address class imbalance in tabular data classification. The authors compare their approach against a broad set of generative baselines including SMOTE, SMOTENC, TVAE, CopulaGAN, CTGAN, CTAB-GAN, CTAB-GAN+, GReaT, and TabDDPM. TVAE, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN are run using implementations from the Synthetic Data Vault library, serving as baseline generators against which EPIC's LLM-based synthesis is evaluated.
paper-epic-effective-prompting-imbalance.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract-tier citing sentences available, so exact experimental role and results table for SDV models could not be verified beyond baseline listing.

paper-enhancing-dementia-risk-screening-.summary: This conference paper investigates whether synthetic data generation can improve machine-learning prediction of dementia risk (MMSE scores) from periodontal examination and blood test measurements collected from 108 participants, validated on an external set of 41. The authors compare three augmentation strategies -- SMOGN, a standard GAN, and CTGAN -- for expanding the small training set to 5000 samples, then train logistic regression, random forest, and DNN models on each. CTGAN-augmented training data yielded the best external-validation prediction accuracy among the methods tested. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run directly as one of the generators whose synthesized data drives the paper's headline results.
paper-enhancing-dementia-risk-screening-.needs: The in-text citation numbering is inconsistent (reference [7] is attributed to SMOGN in one sentence but flagged by metadata as the CTGAN citation, while [8] is explicitly the CTGAN citation in the methods section); treated evidence based on the clearly CTGAN-specific passages.

paper-enhancing-bond-strength-prediction.summary: This paper develops a data-driven model, using data augmentation and explainable AI techniques, to predict bond strength at the interface between ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC) and normal concrete (NC). The work applies machine learning with augmented training data to improve prediction accuracy on a limited experimental dataset. It cites the TGAN paper, presumably in relation to synthetic data generation methods used for augmenting the small dataset, though the evidence does not confirm which technique was actually run.
paper-enhancing-bond-strength-prediction.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether TGAN or a related synthetic data augmentation method was actually run or only cited in passing.

paper-fake-till-you-make-2024.summary: This paper studies how generative machine learning models—GANs and VAEs—can create synthetic tabular transaction data to support decision-making in emerging carsharing programs where real data is scarce, using usage data from a free-floating electric-vehicle carsharing service. The authors show that augmenting real training data with synthetic samples improves predictive modeling of upcoming trips by up to 4.63%. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited as prior work in the synthetic tabular data generation space that frames the study's methodological grounding.
paper-fake-till-you-make-2024.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether the SDV library or a specific SDV synthesizer (e.g., CTGAN, GaussianCopula) was actually run as one of the evaluated generative models, or whether the citation is purely background.

paper-fed-evolver-automated-evolving-202.summary: This paper proposes a federated intrusion detection system for SDN-enabled networks that uses an adversarial autoencoder to adaptively evolve detection models across distributed nodes. The system targets network security in software-defined networking environments, addressing data scarcity or class imbalance issues in intrusion detection datasets. The evidence gives no citing sentence or abstract detail, only that CTGAN's paper is cited, so CTGAN is referenced as related work without confirmed use in the pipeline.
paper-fed-evolver-automated-evolving-202.needs: Full text or citing sentence needed to determine whether CTGAN is run experimentally (e.g., for data augmentation of intrusion detection data) or merely cited in passing.

paper-generative-models-tabular-review-2.summary: Reviews tabular generative modelling for readers coming from engineering design, first laying out notation for mixed continuous and discrete attributes and the model families available, from decision trees and random forests through MLPs, VAEs and GANs to Gaussian processes and Bayesian networks, then organizing the literature by what the generated data is for: differential privacy, missing-value interpolation, data distribution modelling, and data augmentation. Each objective gets a table of reported results by dataset and metric, and the paper closes on four standing difficulties, namely non-normal distributions, imbalanced categories, unstable adversarial training and outliers. CTGAN is placed as the pivot of the distribution-modelling literature: the review credits Xu et al. with preprocessing that handles multi-modal continuous attributes by Gaussian mixture normalization and imbalanced discrete attributes by training-by-sampling, and states that these methods went on to influence several subsequent studies. Nothing is implemented or run anywhere in the review, so the entry records a survey that treats CTGAN as the reference point of its field.

paper-machine-learning-precision-diagnos.summary: This paper presents an integration pipeline that combines multi-omics data with clinical and laboratory values to train machine learning classifiers for autoimmune disease diagnosis, achieving up to 96% prediction accuracy. As part of preprocessing, the authors used the Synthetic Data Vault's GAN model to generate synthetic omics samples for an oversampling strategy addressing class imbalance in disease-specific cytokine/chemokine concentration data. SDV's GAN-based synthesizer is thus run as a component of the data-augmentation pipeline feeding the classification models.
paper-machine-learning-precision-diagnos.needs: The paper names only the generic 'SDV GAN model' without specifying CTGAN or another named synthesizer, so no sdv_concept could be assigned.

paper-predicting-blood-transfusions-coro.summary: This work develops a deep neural network approach, paired with synthetic data generation, to predict blood transfusion needs for coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) patients, addressing data quality issues such as missing values and small sample sizes common in clinical datasets. The available evidence is limited to a single related-work sentence listing prior issues in synthetic/clinical data generation, alongside a citation to the TGAN paper. TGAN is only cited in a list of references discussing data-quality problems, with no indication it was run or extended.
paper-predicting-blood-transfusions-coro.needs: Only a single citing sentence and no abstract or full text were available; cannot confirm whether TGAN/synthetic data methodology was actually implemented or merely cited for context. Industry and use_case inferred from title only.

paper-silofuse-2024.summary: Generates tabular data across silos that cannot pool their records, using latent diffusion rather than a GAN so no raw features cross a boundary. CTGAN and TVAE are among the generators the quantitative analysis measures against.

paper-spatiotemporal-bus-arrival-predict.summary: This paper proposes a ConvLSTM-based model for predicting bus arrival times in data-sparse urban transit systems, particularly in developing economies like India, and augments its training data using Conditional Tabular GANs to address limited Intelligent Transportation System infrastructure. The authors train ConvLSTM on CTGAN-generated synthetic data and test on ground truth, showing improved prediction accuracy, and use the table_evaluator library to assess synthetic data quality. CTGAN, described with its conditional generator and feature-conditioning mechanism, is the core data-augmentation engine underpinning the whole empirical study.
paper-spatiotemporal-bus-arrival-predict.needs: Unclear whether the authors ran the sdv-dev CTGAN package directly or reimplemented the architecture themselves from the described equations; no explicit package name or hyperparameter table is given.

paper-synthetic-generation-handling-imba.summary: This conference paper proposes a fraud-detection pipeline for mobile/e-commerce financial transactions in which a GAN is used to generate synthetic data to augment training sets, followed by edited nearest neighbourhood noise removal and classification with Random Forest, SVM, and logistic regression. The paper cites the CTGAN paper only in a passing technical remark about the GAN min-max objective function, with no library import, hyperparameters, or experimental use found anywhere in the full text outside the reference list. CTGAN is only cited bibliographically to explain the generic GAN objective, never run or engaged with substantively.
paper-synthetic-generation-handling-imba.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the GAN used is SDV's CTGAN implementation or a custom/vanilla GAN architecture, so integration and importance are based only on the abstract-tier citation context.

paper-convolution-neural-network-leak-20.summary: The paper presents an IoT-based Smart Water Grid prototype with sensors monitoring pressure, temperature, flow, pH and turbidity, and develops a 1-D CNN model that simultaneously detects leaks, estimates their size, and locates them from 5-minute time-series chunks, outperforming other machine learning baselines. SDV is mentioned only in passing, as a definitional citation describing it as a validated generative model for relational synthetic data, with no evidence it was used in the study.
paper-convolution-neural-network-leak-20.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so it is unclear whether SDV appears elsewhere with more engagement.

paper-synthetic-set-benchmark-anti-2023.summary: This data descriptor presents SynthAML, a synthetic benchmark dataset for anti-money-laundering (AML) research, built from real transaction and alert data at Spar Nord, a Danish bank, since no public AML datasets exist due to confidentiality constraints. The authors validate that models trained on the synthetic data transfer to real-world performance and discuss open AML research problems the dataset can support. SynthAML is generated entirely using the SDV library's HMA1 multi-table relational synthesizer with Gaussian copulas, run directly (SDV version 0.14.1) to produce the released two-table synthetic dataset.

paper-anonymity-can-help-minority-2023.summary: This paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework for imbalanced multi-label graph node classification, generating virtual minority and unlabeled boundary samples to improve representation learning on graphs with class-imbalanced, multi-label nodes. It is evaluated on several real-world network datasets and outperforms strong baseline models. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of a deep generative model capturing label correlations via probability distribution estimation, without being run or evaluated.
paper-anonymity-can-help-minority-2023.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is actually implemented/run in the oversampling method or is purely a background citation to GANs in general.

paper-synthetic-tabular-generative-adver.summary: This paper proposes a divide-and-conquer strategy for generating synthetic tabular health data that preserves logical relationships between columns, evaluated on a lung cancer registry and two benchmark disease datasets. The method partitions data by class or by column correlation, generates each subset with a GAN-based synthesizer, and recombines the outputs, comparing this against conditional-sampling-based generation across four downstream classifiers. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run directly as the two generative models producing all synthetic data, and the paper evaluates them with shape, pair-trend, and overall quality scores matching SDMetrics' quality report.

paper-wgan-synthetic-tbm-generation-2022.summary: This paper proposes a Wasserstein GAN (WGAN) approach for generating synthetic tunnel boring machine (TBM) operational data, aimed at enabling open research and education while avoiding confidentiality issues tied to real construction-site data. The authors describe and evaluate their WGAN's ability to produce data that is both dissimilar enough to preserve confidentiality and similar enough to remain usable as real data. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer (from the original SDV paper) is only cited in the related-work discussion of prior statistical/probabilistic synthetic data methods and is never run.
paper-wgan-synthetic-tbm-generation-2022.needs: Full text or citing sentence needed to confirm whether SDV is merely cited in related work or used/compared as a synthesizer for TBM data generation.

paper-practical-framework-generate-manag.summary: This paper presents a custom-built application with three modules -- a data generator using user-defined distributions, a flexible relational database, and a filtering/visualization component -- for producing and managing synthetic sensor data for software testing purposes. It surveys existing synthetic data tools in related work, describing CTGAN as 'an open-source project from MIT which is a collection of Deep Learning-based Synthetic Data Generators'. CTGAN is only mentioned and cited as related prior work, not run or used in the authors' own framework.

paper-blockchain-secure-group-collaborat.summary: This paper proposes a blockchain-based architecture combining trusted execution environments, public-key infrastructure, and differentially private synthetic data to let groups of users securely aggregate and share cloud data without exposing raw content. The system's own synthetic data generation is evaluated for utility against real data, but the mechanism used is not tied to a named SDV tool in the given evidence. CTGAN is cited and described in the related-work discussion of tabular generative models, noting its ability to jointly model discrete and continuous columns, without being run in the experiments shown.
paper-blockchain-secure-group-collaborat.needs: Full text does not describe the exact generator used for the paper's own synthetic data experiments, so it is unclear whether CTGAN itself was run beyond being cited as background.

paper-collection-usage-privacy-mobility-.summary: This paper reports on expert interviews with practitioners in enterprises and public administrations to understand how human mobility data is collected, used, and protected under privacy-enhancing methods, finding widespread non-compliance with state-of-the-art differential privacy standards. It categorizes purposes, data sources, and modeling tasks, and lays groundwork for standardized evaluation of privacy methods for mobility data. SDV is mentioned only in passing as an example system for synthetic data models, benchmarks, and metrics that could be extended to the mobility domain.

paper-gdegan-graphical-discriminative-em.summary: This paper proposes GDEGAN, a GAN architecture for tabular data that adds a discriminative embedding module to compress sparse one-hot encodings into a continuous latent space and introduces a graphical-conditional vector to capture attribute correlations, aiming to reduce mode collapse. The authors reuse CTGAN's conditioning method for categorical columns and its generator loss as the basis for their own generator, and also build 'GCTGAN' by applying their graphical conditional vector improvement directly on top of CTGAN, benchmarking extensively against it across simulated and real datasets. CTGAN's mode-specific one-hot handling and conditional vector design are the concept GDEGAN's architecture is built on and extended.
paper-gdegan-graphical-discriminative-em.needs: Unclear whether the CTGAN baseline numbers come from running the sdv-dev package or the authors' own reimplementation, since no library/package name is mentioned explicitly.

paper-har-ctgan-2022.summary: Adapts conditional tabular generation to mobile sensor streams for human activity recognition, where readings are continuous but activity labels are discrete. HAR-CTGAN modifies CTGAN's generator for that setting, and the paper measures how progressively shifting other GANs toward CTGAN changes their output quality.

paper-not-all-datasets-born-2022.summary: This work studies adversarial examples and robustness issues that arise specifically from the heterogeneous mixed-type structure of tabular data, contrasting it with the purely continuous data typically studied in adversarial ML research. It proposes new perspectives or methods for crafting/evaluating adversarial perturbations on such heterogeneous tabular datasets. The paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, apparently as related work on modeling heterogeneous tabular data, without evidence of running the SDV-family CTGAN implementation.
paper-not-all-datasets-born-2022.needs: Full text not obtained; only metadata confirms a citation to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper. Cannot verify whether CTGAN is run, described, or merely listed among related work.

paper-malware-classifier-gan-2022.summary: Reports competition results for improving a malware classifier by generating additional malign samples. CTGAN is used alongside CTAB-GAN, so SDV's synthesizer is one of two conditional tabular generators applied to the same imbalance under contest conditions.

paper-synthetic-comparative-2022.summary: Compares generative approaches for tabular synthesis on the twin criteria of preserving distribution and concealing sensitive values, spanning GAN, VAE, SMOTE and DataSynthesizer. SDV is one of the compared generators, so the library stands for the copula-based branch of the comparison rather than supplying the study's tooling.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-as.summary: This conference paper explores using generative adversarial networks to create or supplement disaggregated population records used in agent-based simulations, addressing bias in survey-derived samples. Using a case study of a 1.1 million person population, the authors show that iterative proportional fitting fits better when using GAN-generated disaggregated records than original census-based ones. The CTGAN model from the SDV library is trained as the generator producing the synthetic disaggregated population, and SDV's metrics library is used to evaluate the results.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-as.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN (Xu and Veeramachaneni 2018) was actually run for comparison or only cited descriptively, nor confirm details of the SDMetrics usage.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-si.summary: This paper compares tabular-based and pictorial-based GAN architectures for balancing an imbalanced Android malware system-call dataset, testing multiple classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, boosting methods, etc.) against GAN-augmented training sets from a Kaggle challenge on malware classification. Among the tabular GAN models it evaluates as candidate data balancers are CTGAN and CopulaGAN, run alongside Vanilla GAN, WGAN, and a pictorial CNN-based GAN. CTGAN and SDV's CopulaGAN are run as evaluation subjects, one of several GAN variants compared for oversampling the minority malware class.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-si.needs: Full text does not clarify whether CTGAN/CopulaGAN were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan packages or a custom implementation; presence of CopulaGAN strongly implies the SDV library was used.

paper-analysis-emotions-eeg-machine-2021.summary: This paper analyzes EEG-based emotional state classification using the DREAMER dataset, applying supervised and unsupervised machine learning to valence/arousal/dominance rankings from 23 subjects. To address the dataset's tabular imbalance, the authors describe using a conditional GAN for tabular data (CTGAN), citing its conditional generator and training-by-sampling approach as a way to overcome imbalanced training data, then analyze the resulting synthetic data. CTGAN's conditional generator and training-by-sampling mechanism are adopted to generate synthetic tabular EEG data, though the citation given is to the earlier 2018 TGAN paper rather than the CTGAN paper.
paper-analysis-emotions-eeg-machine-2021.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented; no code, import, or hyperparameter names are given, and the citation is to the 2018 TGAN paper rather than the CTGAN paper despite the text describing CTGAN-specific features.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ge.summary: This conference paper applies generative adversarial networks to design novel high-entropy alloy (HEA) compositions, framing alloy discovery as a generative modeling problem to speed up materials design over costly experimental synthesis and characterization. The abstract describes a generator/discriminator architecture producing candidate alloy compositions classified as real or fake, without full methodological detail available. The work cites CTGAN and the SDV paper, suggesting SDV-family generative modeling for tabular/compositional data informed their GAN approach, though it is unclear whether the SDV library itself was run.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ge.needs: No full text available; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was actually run or only cited as prior generative-modeling work for tabular data.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ha.summary: This paper presents a comparative study of resampling methods (SMOTE, ROS) versus GAN-based tabular synthesis methods (TGAN, CTGAN, CopulaGAN) for addressing class imbalance in a credit-card default dataset, evaluating downstream classifier performance via ROC curves. It finds resampling methods yield a 27% improvement over the imbalanced baseline, while GAN-based methods produce results similar to the unbalanced data. CTGAN and CopulaGAN, both part of the SDV family, are run as synthetic minority-class generators and directly compared against TGAN and the resampling baselines.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ha.needs: Full text does not explicitly state whether the sdv-dev package was imported or the models were reimplemented; CopulaGAN's presence strongly implies SDV library use, but code-level confirmation is absent.

paper-evaluation-metric-synthetic-genera.summary: This paper proposes a composite evaluation metric for differentially private synthetic data generation, combining macro-statistical similarity and machine-learning utility measures assessed against a privacy budget. The authors test their metric using PrivBayes and DPGroupFields to generate synthetic data from two datasets containing personally identifiable information. The Synthetic Data Vault is mentioned only in passing, in a related-work discussion of Copula-based differentially private methods, and is not run in the experiments.

paper-practical-lessons-generating-synth.summary: This paper explores the use of Bayesian networks to generate synthetic primary care and MIMIC-III healthcare data, addressing transparency, modelling of longitudinal data, and patient re-identification risk. The authors argue graphical models offer more interpretable alternatives to GAN-based approaches for capturing distributions and relationships in sensitive health data. Both the original SDV paper and CTGAN are cited only in the introduction's related-work discussion and reference list, with no evidence they were run.

paper-synthetic-benchmarks-genetic-impro.summary: This short paper proposes a method for constructing synthetic benchmarks for genetic improvement (GI), aiming to circumvent the high cost of evaluating real-world software by generating artificial scenarios with statistics drawn from real cases. The work is a position/method paper describing the approach at a high level, without implementing or running any specific data-synthesis tool. SDV is cited only in a passing background sentence noting that artificial data generation is common in machine learning and data science, with no engagement with its methods.
paper-synthetic-benchmarks-genetic-impro.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the body.

paper-bilstm-networks-context-aware-2020.summary: This paper proposes a BiLSTM+CRF context-aware model to identify and label sensitive information in conversational data, training on a synthetic annotated dataset derived from the P3P standard and evaluating multiple embedding strategies. It achieves strong F1 performance and outperforms Google's DLP system on sensitivity labelling tasks. The SDV paper is cited only in a list of references supporting the claim that synthetic data augmentation reduces effort and mitigates class imbalance, without any evidence that SDV software was run.

paper-generating-evaluating-synthetic-pr.summary: This paper proposes a framework for generating and evaluating synthetic UK primary care data that preserves biological relationships, univariate and multivariate statistical similarity, and patient privacy, demonstrated via a proof-of-concept dataset modelled on CPRD data. The SDV paper is cited only in passing as an example of prior work using generative models to create synthetic relational data, with no library used or engaged with.

paper-kung-faux-pandas-simplifying-2019.summary: This work describes a system aimed at lowering barriers to HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant data sharing, intended to enable reproducibility and other research purposes through synthetic or de-identified data. The abstract and available text give no detail on the system's architecture or evaluation. The SDV project's original synthetic data paper is cited only as one of several references supporting the general concept of algorithmically synthesizing data while preserving multivariate relationships.

It is an edited proceedings collection rather than a single research contribution. None of the five extracted passages around the claimed SDV-family citation mention SDV, CTGAN, or any synthetic-data concept, so the citation link appears to be a metadata artifact with no real connection to the Synthetic Data Vault.

preprint-breaking-quality-privacy-tradeo.summary: This paper proposes DiffICL, an in-context-learning approach to tabular data synthesis that pretrains structural priors across many datasets so that generation from a small target dataset infers a distribution rather than memorizing training samples, improving the quality-privacy tradeoff and downstream data augmentation on 14 real-world datasets. CTGAN and TVAE (both introduced in the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper) are run as baseline generators across all benchmark tables, and the paper's distributional-similarity metrics (Shape and Trend) are drawn from the SDV/SDMetrics quality-report framework. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run as comparison baselines throughout the empirical evaluation, and the SDV-derived Shape/Trend quality metrics are used to score generated data.

preprint-context-conditioned-generative-.summary: This preprint proposes conditional normalizing flows (cNF) to refine sub-national household survey distributions under severe data scarcity, evaluating across eight humanitarian household survey datasets spanning six low- and middle-income countries. The main inferential results rest on the cNF's ability to condition generation on continuous external covariates, a mechanism the authors argue standard tabular generative models lack. As a supplementary benchmark, CTGAN and TVAE, implemented via the SDV library, are run as unconditional baselines against the cNF, comparing fidelity and originality of synthetic survey data.

paper-tabkg-supply-chain-logic-2026.summary: Argues that synthetic supply chain records must preserve the operational logic governing them - temporal orderings, arithmetic dependencies, hierarchical taxonomies and conditional rules - and not only their marginal distributions, and builds a framework that first extracts a column relationship knowledge graph using a multi-LLM ensemble with majority voting and then conditions generation on that graph, so that generated records satisfy the discovered constraints rather than merely resembling real ones statistically. CTGAN is one of four compared generators, included as the widely adopted GAN-based framework for tabular synthesis alongside TabDDPM, TabSyn and GReaT.

preprint-prediction-runtime-parameters-p.summary: This work develops machine learning approaches (gradient boosted regression trees combined with active and generative learning) to predict optimal runtime parameters -- node count and tile size -- for large-scale Coupled-Cluster (CCSD) computations on supercomputers such as Aurora, Frontier, and Perlmutter. To address scarce training data from expensive supercomputer runs, the authors augment their datasets using two synthesizers, explicitly named GaussianCopulaSynthesizer and CTGANSynthesizer, evaluating their impact on runtime-prediction accuracy across all three platforms. SDV's Gaussian Copula and CTGAN synthesizers are run directly as the two generative-learning data-augmentation methods underpinning one of the paper's two main experimental approaches.

preprint-shaping-prior-how-synthetic-202.summary: This paper studies how the design of synthetic pretraining task distributions shapes the quality of tabular foundation models, introducing O'PRIOR, a compositional realism prior combining a hierarchical SCM meta-generator, a modular realism engine, an explicit distribution-shift stress module, and a curriculum-governed generation protocol. Holding architecture, optimizer, and compute fixed, the authors show that varying only the synthetic prior yields substantial gains in downstream accuracy and robustness on real tabular benchmarks. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN-based tabular data generation methods within a broader literature review, and is never run or engaged with further.

preprint-validated-synthetic-patient-gen.summary: This preprint introduces multiplicity-weighted Stochastic Attention (SA), a generative framework based on modern Hopfield networks for synthesizing small longitudinal patient cohorts, applied to 23 patients' coagulation profiles across pregnancy including PCOS and preeclampsia cases. The authors validate SA against statistical, structural, and mechanistic tests, including a blinded coagulation model calibrated on the synthetic data. As a baseline comparison at this small sample size, CTGAN and TVAE (from Xu et al. 2019) are trained on the same 90 per-visit records and shown to suffer mode collapse and fail to capture cross-visit covariance, contrasting with SA's performance.
preprint-validated-synthetic-patient-gen.needs: Unclear whether the authors used the sdv-dev CTGAN/TVAE package directly or their own reimplementation; no import, package name, or SDV-specific hyperparameters (e.g., generator_lr) are given, only epoch counts.

preprint-explanations-linear-post-hoc-20.summary: This paper proposes ILLUME, a post-hoc explainability framework that combines a globally trained surrogate with instance-specific linear transformations learned via a meta-encoder, producing accurate, robust, and computationally efficient feature attributions and decision rules for black-box tabular classifiers. The work is unrelated to synthetic data generation; CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of a generative method enabled by a broader neural-network technique, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-cardiac-risk-generation-2025.summary: Models cardiac rehabilitation as a business process and addresses the small, imbalanced patient records it yields by proposing conditional variational autoencoder variants with supervised and contrastive latent structure, then measuring whether classifiers trained on the augmented sets predict risk better than those trained on the original data. CTGAN is one of three publicly available generators run as the state-of-the-art comparison, with hyper-parameters from its original publication, and the paper reports it failing on this dataset: it achieves low accuracy for the at-risk class and shifts the original distribution despite being conditional.

preprint-measuring-quality-project-light.summary: This is an Airbnb technical paper describing how Project Lighthouse measures the preservation of data quality under anonymization (k-anonymity and p-sensitive k-anonymity), proposing three data quality metrics and a machine-learning-classification framework for empirically justifying metric thresholds to support quantitative data minimization. The paper cites the CTGAN paper (Xu et al., 2019) only in its reference list, with no discussion or use of the method found in the body text examined.
preprint-measuring-quality-project-light.needs: Body text around the citation was not found to discuss CTGAN; treated as an undifferentiated reference-list citation.

preprint-pucktrick-library-making-synthe.summary: This paper introduces Pucktrick, a Python library that deliberately contaminates synthetic datasets with missing values, noise, outliers, mislabeling, duplication, and class imbalance, so that ML models trained on synthetic data can be evaluated for robustness under realistic imperfections. Experiments on financial datasets show that models trained on contaminated synthetic data can outperform those trained on pristine synthetic data. In its related-work discussion the paper describes SDV in detail -- its recursive relational modeling, Gaussian-copula-based distribution modeling, and its table/key noise injection methods -- and also describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator, but neither is run in Pucktrick's own experiments.

paper-structsynth-llm-structure-2025.summary: Splits tabular synthesis into structure discovery and structure-guided generation: a directed acyclic graph is learned from the scarce real data, then supplied to a language model as an explicit blueprint of feature dependencies, so the generated rows respect the discovered structure rather than whatever correlations the model happens to infer, which improves fidelity and downstream utility over both implicit generators and unguided language models when data is thin. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the four deep generative baselines run across six datasets, and the paper's own citation trail attributes both the VAE line and the wider synthesis literature back to the Synthetic Data Vault paper.

paper-task-decoding-eye-movements-2025.summary: Revisits Yarbus's claim that the viewing task can be read off the eye movements, on a dataset small enough that the spatial-temporal classifiers it wants to use cannot be trained directly. Synthetic participants fill the gap, generated by three systems and compared. Two of the three are SDV's — CTGAN and CopulaGAN, the latter existing nowhere outside the library — with Gretel's hosted CTGAN as the third, so SDV is run to produce the augmentation the classification results depend on.

paper-nrgboost-2024.summary: Trains gradient-boosted trees to maximise a local second-order approximation of the likelihood rather than a loss against a supervised target, giving an energy-based generative model that supports single-variable inference at the level of a discriminative boosted-tree model while sampling by Gibbs. TVAE is one of the compared generators, taken from the SDV package and tuned over fifty trials of random search.

preprint-trialsynth-generation-synthetic.summary: TrialSynth is a Variational Autoencoder combined with Hawkes Processes designed to generate synthetic time-sequential clinical trial event data, addressing the challenge of small patient populations where prior static-context synthesizers fall short. The authors benchmark it against seven models including an LSTM VAE, TabDDPM, HALO, and SDV's PARSynthesizer and CTGAN on real-world oncology trial datasets, measuring fidelity, utility, and privacy leakage. SDV's PARSynthesizer (a conditional probabilistic auto-regressive model) and CTGAN are both run as baseline synthesizers, among several others, that TrialSynth is shown to outperform.

preprint-why-llms-bad-synthetic-2024.summary: This paper diagnoses a structural weakness in LLM-based synthetic tabular data generation, showing that autoregressive token generation with random feature-order fine-tuning fails to capture functional dependencies and conditional class-mixtures, and proposes Permutation-aided Fine-tuning (PAFT) to fix this. The authors benchmark PAFT against CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TabSyn, and GReaT on six real and four simulated datasets, evaluating violation rates, ML efficacy, and distributional similarity. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run as baseline generators via the officially released SDV library API, and SDMetrics' quality-report scores (single-column shape, pairwise trends) are used as core evaluation metrics throughout the empirical comparison.

preprint-zgan-outlier-focused-generative.summary: This paper introduces zGAN, a GAN architecture from zypl.ai designed to generate realistic synthetic tabular data enriched with outliers, using covariance-based sampling grounded in Extreme Value Theory to model rare economic events for credit-risk classification tasks. It benchmarks zGAN against several established synthesizers—CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula, PrivBayes, and Synthpop—on private financial and public (Titanic) datasets, measuring classification AUC and correlation preservation. CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN and GaussianCopula are run directly via the SDV library (explicitly citing docs.sdv.dev) with default hyperparameters as comparison baselines against which zGAN's performance and correlation fidelity are evaluated.
preprint-zgan-outlier-focused-generative.needs: The only sentence explicitly matched to the cited tgan-2018 paper (about PSA-GAN/data correlation) does not itself describe SDV library use; the load-bearing SDV usage is evidenced elsewhere in the body (SDV library models section) rather than at the cited sentence itself.

paper-c3-tgan-2023.summary: Argues that GAN-based tabular synthesis ignores explicit attribute correlations and property constraints, so downstream analysis of the synthetic data can reach wrong conclusions even when marginals look right. C3-TGAN adds both to the tabular GAN, a named derivative that extends the architecture rather than applying it.

preprint-time-series-generation-contrast.summary: This paper proposes TimeGCI, a generative framework for time-series data that combines a forward-looking transition policy trained via imitation with a stepwise-decomposable energy model trained by contrastive estimation, aiming to avoid compounding error while preserving joint trajectory distributions. The method is evaluated on real-world datasets using the Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real framework. CTGAN is cited only in a list of references discussing the general difficulty of evaluating synthetic tabular data and the TSTR evaluation standard, without being run or compared against.

preprint-global-measure-simultaneously-e.summary: This preprint proposes a new statistical measure that jointly quantifies the utility-privacy trade-off of synthetic or de-identified datasets, using a relative-distance metric between synthetic and original data plus an accompanying visualization tool. Numerical studies on simulated and real datasets show the measure outperforms existing one-sided utility or privacy metrics. The paper cites the TGAN synthetic data generation method (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) from the SDV family, apparently as related work on synthetic data generation.

preprint-artificial-intelligence-silico-.summary: This review surveys AI and machine learning methods applied to in silico clinical trials, covering clinical simulation, individualized predictive modeling, and computer-aided trial design, with an emphasis on ML problem formulations and data sources for each task. It does not run any generative models itself but cites relevant prior work as part of its broad literature synthesis. CTGAN is cited in the reference list as an example of conditional GAN modeling of tabular data, with no experiment or engagement in the body text.

preprint-generating-synthetic-text-evalu.summary: This preprint develops a framework for adapting natural language generation models to produce synthetic text datasets with known causal effects, using it to empirically compare four recently-proposed methods for estimating causal effects from text data. In its introduction, the authors cite prior uses of synthetic data for exploring edge cases and low-resource settings in predictive tasks, listing 'The Synthetic Data Vault' (Patki et al., 2016) among several such references without further engagement or use.
